findings: The November method guide retains the Italy customer location and EUR presentment from May, while the eligible business account list grows from 20 to 37 entries and explicitly covers domestic and cross-border. New 19–21 and 64–82 describe merchant and platform/marketplace (Connect), B2C only, provisional instant access (line 12), and EUR 0.50–999,999.99 transaction bounds. May old 12–38, 52–75,181–185 gave 20 business locations and no such min/max locators. The 17 additional listed locations are AU, BG, CA, CH, CZ, DK, GB, HK, HU, JP, LI, NO, PL, RO, SE, SG and US. This is documentation scope, not proof of an account's access.

November changes May no recurring to reusable and recurring supported, with PaymentIntents including setup_future_usage, SetupIntents and off-session payments and Billing/Invoicing supported. May already linked Subscriptions in Get started while describing no recurring (old 28–30,98–105), so keep dated internal ambiguity rather than imputing a past actual recurring integration. In the older acceptance guide checkout matrices list payment mode only, no Setup/Subscription (extra old acceptance 18–32,95–109). November same acceptance root is a selector (extra November acceptance 1–20), not revalidation. Versioned June 24 Dahlia changelog 1–26 adds recurring, setup and payment intents, and subscriptions/invoices, scoped to its documented API surfaces. Wallet concept 29 and 319,327 and source 21–23 need separate dated treatment. The May 8, 2026 cross-method wallet product matrix header/row (raw/stripe-payment-method-support-2025.md 184,199) also marks Subscriptions, Invoicing and Customer Portal unsupported, while the May 8 Satispay method guide links Subscriptions. The November 7 cross-method wallet header/row (raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-payment-method-support-2026-11-07.md 188,203) still marks all three unsupported, in conflict with the November method Billing, Invoicing and Customer Portal cells (194–208) and with the versioned June 24 Dahlia Subscriptions/Invoices support at lines 9–17. This conflict leaves specific Checkout variants and individual account eligibility unresolved.

November Mandates (164–182) describe customer authorization directly in Satispay and Stripe's automatic recording in Checkout/Payment Element, so captured guide says no additional mandate language in custom payment flows. Stripe stores Mandate associated with PaymentMethod. For SetupIntent use its mandate ID to retrieve details; for PaymentIntent use saved payment_method ID for later payments rather than expecting a top-level mandate. Customer revocation in Satispay triggers mandate.updated, prevents future use and is distinct from merchant detachment to stop use. Saved method and mandate do not prove later payment success.

May manual capture yes persists (old 44–50; new 86–97), with explicit partial yes and multi/over-capture and specified authorization adjustments no. November’s depicted checkout places selection, hosted redirect, either phone request or QR scan, app approval, then immediate confirmation/return (new 209–229), while headline and metadata distinguish immediate outcome notification from standard payout (new 9–14). In a separate manual-capture path, customer approval does not establish captured funds. November matrix also details UI/product limits including no ECE/PMME, Managed Payments or Terminal, alongside in-app, Connect and API routes (new 184–208,239–243).

Old 107–124 lists 13 specifically named categories and a discretion catch-all. November adds coded restrictions and eligibility classes, with 33 table rows, all prohibited in the captured list (new 22–62). Changes in labels or omitted rows such as Automobile Associations alone do not prove any particular category is now permitted. Source 51 and concept 325 blur the old catch-all and named count, and omit the November code-based list.

May 126–148 gave 12 calendar days to provide evidence, disputes such as fraud, double payments and order/amount mismatch, Stripe hold and refund-to-balance if merchant wins. November 105–108,125–162 gives full disputes only and 120-calendar-day customer filing from purchase, merchant 15 calendar days from creation, provider final decision within 25 calendar days of creation, notifications, disputed-balance hold and Dashboard/API evidence route. November 99–123 retains 180-day asynchronous full/partial refunds up to five minutes and failure restoring balance plus alternate refund. It adds noncancelable, never reversal, return to wallet balance on refund, and status tracking. Source line 35 should present events as final status notifications supported by the Refund object's separate succeeded/failed states, not a rule that every refund.updated alone proves success.

May Connect requires satispay_payments active on platform and selected connected accounts, and lays out five charge-type descriptor routes (old 159–179). November retains Connect and route-dependent platform versus connected-account label and adds default/app descriptor, PaymentIntent statement_descriptor and Payment Links/Checkout payment_intent_data.statement_descriptor (new 231–237). Absence of old capability detail from the method overview does not withdraw it. Old demo disappears and UI labels, layout and links change; those are presentation/navigation changes unless a new capability claim is separately stated.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-satispay-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-satispay-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-satispay.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/satispay`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/satispay describes a reusable EUR wallet for Italy customers with eligible business accounts in 37 listed places, domestic/cross-border B2C, provisional access, and EUR 0.50–999,999.99 limits. Customers choose Satispay, open its hosted flow, use phone or QR, approve in app and return. The overview depicts immediate confirmation with standard payout; separate manual and partial capture support does not make app authorization proof of capture (old raw lines 8-50, new raw lines 9-21 and 64-108, new raw lines 209-229). Customers authorize future debits directly with Satispay; Stripe records a mandate linked to the PaymentMethod. SetupIntent retrieval uses mandate ID, PaymentIntent saving uses payment_method, and revocation triggers mandate.updated with later use blocked. The merchant can instead detach the method (new raw lines 164-208). November also retains asynchronous refunds and adds wallet-only non-reversal handling and noncancelability. Disputes have a 120-day filing window, 15 days for evidence and a 25-day decision window. source-stripe-satispay.md preserves May's manual capture and refund terms, but its 20-location, no-recurring and 12-day evidence facts require May dating (old raw lines 52-75 and 126-179, new raw lines 99-162).
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/satispay, substantive November changes are a 20-to-37 business-account list expansion with explicit B2C and domestic/cross-border coverage, amount bounds, recurring and mandate support, partial capture documentation, prohibited MCC table, extended dispute evidence window and new clocks, and refund destination/cancelability/reversal rules (old raw lines 28-75 and 107-157, new raw lines 11-108 and 109-182). May's no-recurring status already coexisted with a Subscriptions link, while the May cross-method wallet matrix lines 184 and 199 mark Subscriptions, Invoicing and Customer Portal unsupported. The November cross-method wallet matrix lines 188 and 203 retains those negatives, in conflict with the November method page's Billing, Invoicing and Customer Portal cells and the June 24 Dahlia versioned Subscriptions and Invoices additions at lines 9–17 (new raw lines 194-208). Specific Checkout variant and individual account eligibility remain unresolved. Preserve the dated May Checkout mode limits from the acceptance guide and the 2026-06-24.dahlia release scope, without applying either uniformly. The November acceptance root provides routes only. Italy/EUR, standard payout, manual capture, 180-day refund and May platform/selected connected account capability and charge-specific descriptor mapping remain dated evidence (old raw lines 32-50 and 150-185, new raw lines 9-14 and 93-123 and 231-237). Reordering, markup and demo or link presentation provide no proof of removal. Update source-stripe-satispay.md and preserve the May raw, root-to-Stripe index and reciprocal Stripe Wallets concept and source route, plus distinct acceptance and future setup routes.
